title: Xanthe and the Salt
premise: When the crown of Vael declares a purge of the gifted, Ines Eriksen flees his master's burning cottage and falls in with a smuggler caravan carrying a strange cargo: a sealed lantern that holds the soul of Prince Aldric, sold to the court beneath Thornfell to keep the last dragon's fire alive. Ines, whose own gift is small and despised, discovers he alone can hear the soul calling its name. To free it, he must descend into the salt courts, bargain with a dragon who has forgotten she was ever anything else, and choose between reclaiming his stolen identity and saving the boy-king whose soul burns in the flame. He frees the soul at the cost of his own gift — and finds that belonging was never something magic could give him.
about_author: J. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write about borders, both drawn on paper and drawn through the heart.

chapters.title: The Burning Hedge
chapters.summary: Ines Eriksen watches from a smuggler's ridge as crown soldiers burn his master's cottage, hunting the gifted. POV: Ines. The emotional beat is grief sharpened into survival instinct; he runs not toward safety but along the only roads he knows, carrying nothing but his master's stolen grimoire and a name he no longer trusts himself to answer to.

chapters.title: Caravan of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Ines buys passage with smuggler captain Odile Vane, hiding his gift among her crew of outcasts. He notices the sealed iron lantern in the cargo hold hums when he nears it. POV: Ines. The beat is wary belonging — for the first time he is among people like him, yet he lies to them, and the lie sits heavy as the lantern grows louder in his dreams.

chapters.title: What the Lantern Sings
chapters.summary: Ines secretly opens his gift to the lantern and hears a boy's voice: Prince Aldric, soul-sold to the court beneath the mountain to feed the dying dragon-fire that warms the realm. POV: Ines, with interludes of the soul's fragmented memories. The beat is horrified compassion — the enemy king is a child, and Ines must decide whether mercy is worth treason.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Odile reveals she knows what Ines is and offers a deal: help her steal the lantern for sale to the salt court's rivals, or she turns him in. POV: Odile. The beat is moral compromise — Odile's pragmatism masks grief for a sister the court consumed, and Ines sees his own future in her hardened face.

chapters.title: The Hunt Comes to Thornfell
chapters.summary: Crown witchfinders ambush the caravan at the Salt Gate pass; half the crew dies covering the lantern's escape. Ines's gift flares publicly for the first time, marking him. POV: Ines. The beat is guilt and resolve — belonging purchased with other people's blood is no belonging at all, and he vows to finish what the dead started.

chapters.title: Descent into Salt
chapters.summary: Guided by the soul's song, Ines descends abandoned mine-shafts into the crystalline court beneath Thornfell, where courtiers of salt trade memories as currency. POV: Ines. The beat is disorientation and temptation — the court offers him a new identity, any identity, painlessly bought, and he nearly forgets his own name.

chapters.title: The Dragon Who Forgot
chapters.summary: Ines reaches the dragon Vess, now a furnace of habit and salt, sustained by Aldric's burning soul. She remembers nothing but warmth. POV: alternating Ines and Vess. The beat is devastating tenderness — Vess begs him not to take the fire, because without it she will finally die, and Ines understands power always eats someone.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Ash
chapters.summary: Ines offers the court a trade: his own gift, freely given, in exchange for Aldric's soul. The salt magistrates accept, savoring corruption offered willingly. POV: Ines. The beat is sacrifice with teeth — he surrenders the thing that made him hunted, hated, and himself, discovering that giving it up is the first truly free choice he has made.

chapters.title: The Last Guttering
chapters.summary: As the lantern opens, Vess chooses to spend her final fire not on the realm but on burning the salt court's throne, freeing every caged memory. Ines carries Aldric's soul up through collapsing tunnels. POV: Ines. The beat is triumphant loss — the climax costs the dragon her life, the court its power, and Ines everything magical he had.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: Ines returns Aldric's soul to the boy-king, who ends the hunt for the gifted. Giftless now, Ines rejoins Odile's diminished crew as an ordinary hand. POV: Ines. The beat is quiet resolution — belonging arrives not as reward but as choice, and when someone asks if he misses his gift, he tastes salt and says only, 'I remember the way.'
